subject: SLO scouting: latency & streaming PoC plan for LumenRx
messages:
From: Oliver Trent <oliver@lumenrx.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from this morning — latency & streaming constraints

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and a few clarifying datapoints from our side so you can help sketch a workable PoC and rough cost envelope.

Key constraints we mentioned today:
- Target SLO: 95th %ile end-to-end response latency <= 150ms for streaming chat (token-by-token UX)
- Typical session concurrency: 60-80 active streaming sessions during peak; want headroom to 100
- Throughput: steady 200 requests/sec (avg), spiky bursts up to 450 req/sec for short windows
- Prompts: average user prompt (~40 tokens), plus streaming generation up to ~150 tokens; some long-context retros (up to 2k tokens) for a small percentage of queries
- Model preference: baseline instruction-tuned 7B for cost reasons; fallback 13B for complex queries that need higher quality
- Strict cost target: monthly inference spend below our internal cap (we can share numbers after NDA)

What we can share right now: a small sample payload JSON (attached), and a Drive link to our synthetic traffic profile.

As next steps: would appreciate a one-page PoC plan that calls out measurable acceptance criteria (latency targets, concurrency behavior, workload shape), a short list of levers you expect to tune (batching, cache, quant, routing), and an estimate for a 2-week dedicated PoC (hardware profile + rough cost).

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Trent
Sr. Product Manager, LumenRx Health
oliver@lumenrx.com

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the sample payloads. Good to see the throughput + concurrency numbers; that helps narrow the path for a compact PoC. Below is a proposed PoC outline and the specific inputs we'll need to size and estimate. Happy to iterate.

Proposed 2-week PoC (high level)
1) Goals & acceptance criteria
   - Verify p95 streaming latency <= 150ms for the 7B baseline under target concurrency (60–80) and bursts up to 450 r/s
   - Ensure tail latency graceful degradation: p99 <= 400ms or documented fallback behavior
   - Validate functional parity for 90% of prompts vs current model (we'll use your eval set)

2) What we'll measure
   - Token-level latency breakdown (network, tokenizer, generation loop, finalization)
   - Throughput vs concurrency matrix (end-to-end)
   - Cost per 1k tokens and per conversation at target load

3) Primary cost/perf levers we plan to exercise
   - Continuous batching with short hold windows (e.g., 10–30ms) to reduce per-token overhead
   - Prefix/KV cache for repeating system prompts or common context blocks
   - Model variants + quantization profiles (int4 for 7B candidate; int8 or mixed-precision for 13B fallback)
   - Per-route routing: send latency-sensitive calls to reserved pool, overflow to burst pool or fallback model

4) PoC test harness & ticketing
   - We'll deploy a lightweight harness that replays your sample payloads with configurable concurrency and tokenization to your S3 dataset.
   - We request your acceptance eval set and a list of ~20 representative conversations for quality checks.

5) Deliverables (end of PoC)
   - Performance report: latency percentiles, cost breakdown by lever, recommendation for production config
   - Runbook with suggested batching/cache/quant profiles and a templated autoscaling policy

Immediate asks from your team
- Share the eval set + 1:1 traffic split (synthetic vs production-like)
- Confirm willingness to provision a short-lived reserved pool for testing (we can provide baseline configs)
- Any regulatory constraints (data residency, redaction) we should account for

Attachments: I dropped a draft mutual action plan I can populate with dates once we agree on start. See attached: MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_LumenRx_v1.xlsx

I'll loop Ben in with a recommended baseline config next — Ben, I sketched a couple of options under the 7B/13B split.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai

Adding some technical notes / suggested starting points based on the numbers:

Baseline hypothesis (fast path)- Model: 7B instruction-tuned, quantized to int4 for the hot path
- Serving: dedicated pool with KV cache enabled for repeated system prompts and static context. This avoids repeated prefix decoding for every session
- Batching: continuous batching with 10ms collect window at 80 concurrent streams; tune to 20ms if p95 drifts above target
- Streaming behavior: token-by-token flush with small frame sizes (10–20 tokens) to keep UX responsive; combine with small prefetch on first token to reduce handshake overhead

Fallbacks & routing- If token backlog increases beyond X ms, route new sessions to 13B int8 fallback (slower but higher quality) or to a burst pool with relaxed latency SLOs
- Consider an admission control policy to preserve p95 for existing streams (reject or slow new sessions under extreme load)

Instrumentation & tests- We'll run an initial matrix: concurrency [20, 40, 60, 80, 100], burst shapes (sustained vs spiky), and payload lengths [short, mid, long].
- We need your tokenizer choice and sample prompts to ensure consistent token count measurement.

I've attached a short CSV with perf-profile baselines based on our internal sim for similar workloads — treat numbers as starting points.

Attachment: perf-profiles.csv

If you can confirm the PoC start window (Sofia suggested April 18), I'll size the reserved pool and send a cost delta for a 2-week run.

- Ben
